k_selection.global_silhouette_peak_note: degenerate active-vs-dormant binary split; excluded from selection
k_selection.reason: Global silhouette peaks at k=2 (0.3586), but that is a DEGENERATE active-vs-dormant binary split, not a segmentation, so we exclude k<3. Among business-meaningful k the inertia elbow is k=5, and k=5 is ALSO a local silhouette maximum (0.2649 > k=4:0.2511 and > k=6:0.2379). Both signals endorse k=5, and it isolates the thin high-value tier the business needs — so k=5 is the honest choice.

kmeans_vs_rfm_note: RFM-quantile 'Champions' (R5-F5-M5) = 336 customers holding $3,774,233 (45.3% of revenue). KMeans VIP cluster = 700 customers holding $5,537,125 (66.5%). RFM forces a rigid 1/125 grid and treats each axis independently, so it can miss customers who are extreme on money but merely good on frequency. KMeans learns the joint geometry (post-log) and isolates the thin ultra-VIP tier that actually carries a disproportionate revenue share — the segment a business most needs to protect.
